rawFindings.title: Incorrect path resolution in PostAsset.path virtual property
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug) which constructs a file system path. The changed code uses url.resolve(post.path, this.slug) which treats inputs as URLs and performs URL resolution. This can alter the resulting path unexpectedly, especially if `post.path` is a filesystem path rather than a URL. This changes semantics and may break path resolution within the application.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert the change at line 22 to use pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug) as in the original code to correctly join file paths relative to `public_dir`.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect URL resolution in PostAsset.path virtual property
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaces pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug) with url.resolve(post.path, this.slug) when computing PostAsset.path. url.resolve treats the second argument as an absolute URL path if it starts with a slash, or merges the base with the relative path otherwise. Unlike pathFn.join, url.resolve performs URL resolution semantics which may alter the resulting path unexpectedly, especially when the slug contains special characters or spaces. rawFindings.suggestion: Revert the return statement in PostAsset.path virtual getter to 'return pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug);' to preserve original file path joining behavior as documented with comment referencing issue #1562.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect path joining in PostAsset.path virtual
rawFindings.explanation: The original code used path.join to join post.path and this.slug which generates a file system path, not a URL path. The new code uses url.resolve which treats post.path as a base URL and resolves this.slug as a relative URL. However, url.resolve is designed for URLs and can drop parts if this.slug starts with a slash or behave unexpectedly with some strings, potentially breaking the returned path.
rawFindings.suggestion: Replace url.resolve with a safer method for joining URL paths that does not remove base path segments unexpectedly, such as a custom join that ensures proper slashes, or validate inputs before using url.resolve.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect usage of url.resolve for file paths instead of path.join
rawFindings.explanation: The code changes line 23 from using pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug) to url.resolve(post.path, this.slug). The url.resolve function is intended for resolving URLs, not filesystem paths. post.path is a file path relative to public_dir, so path.join is appropriate. Using url.resolve may lead to unexpected path resolution, especially if post.path is not a full URL.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert line 23 back to using pathFn.join(post.path, this.slug) for correct filesystem path joining.
